subject.title: [Feature]: First-class org/team deployment — workspace scaffolding, RBAC, and deployment manifests

question: Which parts of this org/team deployment umbrella should OpenClaw core own now, and should the Gateway trust model grow a first-class team or tenant RBAC boundary?
rationale: The answer defines public security, config, CLI, session, and upgrade contracts, and current docs explicitly avoid promising hostile multi-tenant isolation inside one Gateway.

options.title: Decompose under this umbrella
options.body: Keep this issue open and approve narrow sub-issues only after the threat model, config surface, and migration behavior are explicit.

options.title: Route setup outward, keep core APIs
options.body: Keep core focused on missing auth/session/tool-policy APIs while scaffolding and deployment manifests live in plugins, docs, or external tooling.

options.title: Decline first-class team mode for now
options.body: Close the umbrella only after documenting separate gateways, trusted proxy, and per-agent profiles as the supported isolation pattern.

recommendation.title: Decompose under this umbrella
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open and approve narrow sub-issues only after the threat model, config surface, and migration behavior are explicit.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent history on the trust-model docs and scoped conversation capability seam that would anchor this decision.
